I'm all in on the Switch. Mostly because of Zelda: Breath of the Wild. Preordered my shit the night after their big Tokyo reveal show.

I did get to try a bunch of games at PAX South to get a taste.

ARMS was ok, but I'll pass. The controls were a lot better than I thought they'd be. Nothing like just flailing in Wii Boxing. This probably would be a great multiplayer game. Just not one I can imagine paying full price for. When it hits $20 or $30 or whatever the Nintendo Selects line is, I may get it.

Splatoon 2 was a lot of fun. I never played the original Splatoon, so I have no idea how it's different, if it's different, or any of that. Looked identical to me. Not sure why this is Splatoon 2 instead of Splatoon: Deluxe Edition like they're doing with Mario Kart 8. Still probably won't get it just because online shooters aren't really my thing anymore.

Snipperclips was a blast. This will be an instant buy for me. The art style is goofy and kinda cute but not entirely saccharine. Plus the way the puzzles make your cooperate is unique and even with what little I played, contained a lot of emergent shenanigans. I can't wait to sit my girlfriend down in front of it.

Has Been Heroes, which I think is multi platform, but I played on the Switch, was a ton of fun too. This was actually much better than I thought from seeing the trailer. Another day 1 buy for me whenever it comes out. I think a week or two after launch. I asked the booth worker if it was available on launch day, and he said it was, but I think he might have been wrong. Everything else I've read says it's later. Regardless, whenever it comes out, I'm on it.

And I even got to play Breath of the Wild, which blew me away. Having replayed Twilight Princess and currently replaying Skyward Sword, it's amazing what a tonal shift Breath of the Wild is. The best comparison I can make, is that Breath of the Wild is to the original Zelda, what Doom 2016 is to Doom 1993. It's just this radical re-imagining of the original source material, that somehow captures the spirit of it just right, even if the mechanics are completely different. But, I only had 20 minutes with it, so we'll see what the rest of the game turns out to be like.

Some friends of mine say a system has to have 7 games they want before they'll buy it. I'm not sure when the Switch will hit that for me. But I'm confident it will eventually. I'm also really excited about Octopath Traveller, Xenoblade 2, Mario Odyssey, Fire Emblem Warriors and Dragon Quest Heroes.

I'm kind of happy at the small number of launch titles because it means there's no reason for me not to hold off until fall when my brother gets back from out of state. I don't trust Nintendo enough to pull off online multiplayer, so I'd rather cut my teeth on the local multiplayer and see what happens with the rest later.
